Alex.feeling: Messy and tense: the Turkey and Falcon egg counts got tangled, and I already changed my position once.

Blair.feeling: Tense and confusing: the egg counts were hard to reconcile, and Drew's rush to call a vote on me without explaining his Tit visit makes me uneasy.

Casey.feeling: Confusing and contradictory so far: the egg counts keep shifting as players revise their stories, and I've been wrong about Turkey mechanics myself.

Drew.feeling: Messy and contradictory: several players keep changing their stories, and I'm not sure who is lying.

Ellis.feeling: Messy round: several players have shifted or contradicted their claims, and the egg counts are hard to reconcile, so I'm not confident about anyone yet.

Alex.confusing: The Turkey rule was the most confusing: I misread that a Turkey gains an egg per visitor, when it lays eggs in each visitor's nest, and that nearly got Blair eggsecuted. The egg-token timing also made it hard to tell which visits had already happened.
Alex.fun: Round 2, when my Kookaburra check exposed Ellis as the Sphinx and the table followed my lead to vote them out. Finding a Meowfia cat with one visit felt satisfying.
Alex.change: I'd make the dawn report clearer about who visited whom, so players can cross-check claims without reading egg changes as rule puzzles. I'd also make Turkey and Falcon egg effects spelled out in the report.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I publicly accused Blair on a misreading of the Turkey rule and cast a vote for Blair before checking it. I should have reread the rule and asked for clarification before accusing anyone.

Blair.confusing: Egg counts for Turkey and Falcon were hard to read: I first assumed a Turkey gains eggs from visits, when it actually lays eggs in its visitors' nests. That mix-up made my honest Turkey claim look false for a while.
Blair.fun: Round 2, when my Meowfia team won by throwing six cards at Drew and banked 47 points. The vote split was close enough that the timing mattered.
Blair.change: I would make dawn reports state exactly which animals visited you and what each one did, so players can check claims without reconstructing the rules.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I threw my card at Drew, who was Farm, instead of Finley, who was the Meowfia Sphinx. I would throw at Finley and watch the Sphinx's claims more closely.

Casey.confusing: The Turkey rule was the hardest to follow: I wrongly argued a Turkey gains eggs from visits, when it's the visitors who gain eggs, and the egg-token and throw-count bookkeeping made the day hard to track.
Casey.fun: Round 2, when my Eagle visit to Ellis returned three visitors and three eggs, and the table split into a fierce argument over who was really Meowfia.
Casey.change: I'd make the dawn reports name the visitors' roles or egg sources more clearly, so players can check claims without misreading the rules.
Casey.regret: In Round 1 I threw my Wild at Finley and then pushed suspicion onto Finley with weak reasoning; I should have stayed quiet and kept my nest intact instead of drawing attention.

Drew.confusing: I misread the Turkey rule for a while: I thought a Turkey gained eggs from its own visits, when it actually lays eggs in each visitor's nest. That made the Blair and Alex egg counts look contradictory for most of the day.
Drew.fun: Round 2, when Ellis claimed Sphinx and my Hawk egg from visiting Ellis backed up the cat claim, the table turned on Ellis quickly.
Drew.change: Put each egg's source in the dawn report, so players can see which visit produced which egg and don't have to reverse-engineer the Turkey and Falcon math.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I called for a vote on Blair, who was Farm, before checking the egg math. I would instead have asked Alex and Casey to explain their egg counts first and kept my throw on Ellis, the Meowfia who was pushing to clear Blair.

Ellis.confusing: The Turkey and Falcon egg accounting was hard to follow on the day, since a Turkey gains an egg per visitor and a Falcon gains only when its target visited no one. I also couldn't tell whether an egg token counted as a card gain before the vote.
Ellis.fun: Round 1 went well: my Meowfia side won with a full nest of five cards banked for 23 points, and Casey and I kept the Farm table split on who was lying.
Ellis.change: I'd make the day less rushed, since the CAW CAW calls ended discussion before players could check claims against each other.
Ellis.regret: In Round 3 I threw all three of my cards at Blair, a Farm player, instead of keeping them, which cost me the chance to bank a safer total. Knowing Blair was Turkey, I'd have held my cards and voted with the evidence instead of pushing a vote.

Finley.confusing: The Owl and Turkey reports were hard to read, since a Turkey gains an egg per visitor and a Falcon gains only when it visited no one. Several players got these wrong in the day, including me.
Finley.fun: In round 3, as the Meowfia Sphinx, I helped eggsecute Drew, a Farm Tit, while Blair and Ellis were checking each other's Turkey and Mouser stories. Watching the table untangle the nest counts was a lot of fun.
Finley.change: I would make the egg-count reports clearer, so every player can tell which visits produced which egg changes without working out the arithmetic.
Finley.regret: In round 1 I threw at Casey, but Ellis was the Mouser and threw 5 cards at me, which decided the vote. I should have pressed harder on Ellis's Mouser claim, since it contradicted Casey's Floofer claim and Ellis had no check on anyone.

review.title: The Wrong Eggsecution
review.headline: Meowfia won every round by dumping whole nests on innocents.
review.summary: Round 1 ended with Ellis, a Meowfia, throwing his whole nest at Finley and banking 23 points. In round 2 the table correctly pinned Ellis. Blair, the other cat, threw six cards at Drew and flipped the vote, which made Blair the leader with 48. In round 3 the table tangled itself over Turkey and Falcon egg math, and Meowfia won again. Blair finished first with 49, ahead of Ellis on 46.

rounds.recap: Farm read Casey as Meowfia after Casey openly claimed Floofer. Ellis, the other Meowfia, threw his whole 5-card nest at Finley. That beat Farm's split votes on Casey, so Finley died and Meowfia won. Ellis banked 23.

Ellis claimed Sphinx, and Drew's Hawk egg confirmed him as Meowfia. Four Farm players threw small cards at Ellis. Blair, the hidden Mouser, threw six cards at Drew and outvoted them. Drew was eggsecuted and Blair banked 47.

Blair was Farm Turkey. The table first called his claim false because players misread what a Turkey does, then corrected themselves late. Farm split its throws between Drew and Ellis, and Finley's three cards helped push Drew out. Meowfia won, with Ellis banking 22 and Finley 12.

highlights.text: Ellis throws his whole nest at Finley, a Farm player, and wins 23 points while the table argues about Casey.
Blair stays silent, then throws six cards at Drew and beats a nearly unanimous Farm vote on Ellis.
Four independent signals (Sphinx claim, Hawk egg, Eagle list, Kookaburra check) all point at Ellis, and Farm still loses the round.
The table turns on Blair over a Turkey misread, then reverses itself in the final beat.

confusions.what: Claimed Owl visitors info that his report did not give, then retracted it.
Said a Turkey gains eggs from visitors. A Turkey lays eggs in its visitors' nests.
Said Blair's unchanged nest disproved Turkey, and later explained his +2 incorrectly before fixing it.
Pushed a vote on Blair using the same Turkey misread.
Repeated the Turkey misread, and said a Falcon's +2 did not fit a visit.
Used the same wrong Turkey logic early on.
Claimed Floofer openly as a Meowfia, apparently mistaking it for a safe claim.

worked: Egg tokens plus visit reports gave real cross-checking evidence in round 2: the Eagle list, Hawk egg and Kookaburra check all agreed.
Throw counts being public made Blair's six-card throw readable afterward, and it created a real swing.
The Turkey gave a good puzzle in round 3, since an unchanged nest looked like a lie.
problems: Votes are card counts, so one Meowfia dumping a whole nest beats several Farm players throwing one or two cards. Fix: cap throws per player, or make each throw count as one vote.
Winning throws bank full card value, so round 1 Ellis took 23 and round 2 Blair took 47. That decided the whole game in single rounds. Fix: cap banked value or reduce the high-card payoff.
Farm players threw tiny cards for safety, which made the Farm vote weak and let Meowfia dumps win. This is a lack of incentive to commit.
The Turkey's reversed egg rule confused nearly everyone and nearly sank an honest Farm player. Fix: add a wording reminder, or have the dawn report show the Turkey who visited it.
Quiet Meowfia with no coordination and no cost for dumping cards made the round-1 and round-2 votes feel predetermined, so the deduction mattered little.
